edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Fermentable beta-glucans can be converted by gut microbes into short-chain fatty acids, including propionate, especially when baseline fiber intake is low.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2021 Bai meta analysis in Food Funct already points to beta-glucan tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.

evidence.notes: Effects of cereal fibers on short-chain fatty acids in healthy subjects and patients: a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
